judgments.concern: The scenario names which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred, and the handling process uses that distinction while the scene can still change. Ranking this capture's DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements, admitting at most the count this capture will pose, and placing every remaining candidate on the deferred vector is that split for this array. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet and the other candidates in this array stay deferred. The user did not name Stage2Admission, a caller-chosen count, an empty list returning both vectors empty, or an unknown strategy throwing. The scenario states no rule for how many candidates this capture poses. The changing-scene sentence is temporal: a later frame can already have moved, so the split belongs to this capture. It states no rule that the count itself changes because the scene can move. Each candidate keeps its source_index, the slot extract_detection_candidates already stored. The deferred vector stays with the caller. The summary does not place the admitted candidate or the deferred candidates on a result the handling process reads. PalletPoseStamped is that pose result, and it still carries neither a sent index nor a deferred list. The two early returns in on_pair still publish nothing, and a failed estimate still publishes only the failure diagnostic. Width, height, and depth stay unpublished. The pose that is published is still the face of the one admitted pallet.

The scenario names which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred, for the handling process, while the scene can still change. Sending stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and writing that candidate's source index together with the source indices of the other class-matched candidates onto PalletPoseStamped, is both sides of that named split on the pose result that process reads. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture; a later frame can already be a different scene. The user named the split. The part they did not name is that both lists sit on PalletPoseStamped, the pose result for the AGV controller. The same two lists on the failure diagnostic cover the path that publishes no pose. The scenario states no rule that a failed estimate must still publish PalletPoseStamped. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are: an empty candidate list has no split to write, and a depth image that does not convert already has a chosen candidate and deferred candidates that are dropped. Stage 2 still runs once. The scenario states no rule that every detected pallet must be posed. Width, height, and depth stay unpublished. The pose that is published is still the face centre and yaw of the one candidate this strategy sends.

The scenario names a pallet pose and which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred, while the scene can still change. It states no rule that this capture sends two faces, and no rule that the faces with the largest area_px are the pallets the vehicle handles. select_detection already returns one candidate, highest_confidence by score then area, or largest_area by area then score. Sending the two class-matched faces with the largest area_px, breaking ties by higher score and then by lower source index, is a ranking the user did not name. Each success publishes its own PalletPoseStamped from this capture, so one pair can produce two poses. A face that was sent through stage 2 and whose estimate fails is absent from those poses and absent from the deferred marks, which are only the candidates that were not admitted. Each deferred candidate is published as its source index with this pair's RGB and depth stamps. That stamp binding is what the changing-scene sentence requires of a mark. The scenario states no rule for which message carries that index. A pair with fewer than two candidates admits every candidate and defers none. Width, height, and depth stay unpublished.
